priceSnapshot.note: Price is 80,779.1, up 5.42 percent on the 24-hour open of 76,629.4 and 462.5 points above the morning handover at 80,316.6. The breakout held and then confirmed itself. Morning published an add gate at 80,555.4 requiring a SETTLED 1H close; three consecutive hours have now settled above it - 14:00 UTC at 80,946.8, 15:00 UTC at 80,728.7 and 16:00 UTC at 80,849.0 - so the gate did not merely fire, it was defended. The session high is 81,267.0, printed in the 16:30 UTC quarter-hour, and price has spent the four hours since the vertical bar oscillating in a 698-point band between 80,568.6 and 81,267.0. That is a consolidation on top of the break rather than a reversal off it. The single most important number this run is not the price: open interest on the BTC-USDT perp is 2,428,535,885 USD against 2,323,868,439 at the morning read, up 4.50 percent in under four hours. A short squeeze alone REDUCES open interest because shorts are being closed out. Open interest rising by 104.7 million USD while price rises means new positions are being opened into the move, which is the confirmation morning explicitly said it was waiting for. Against that, the extension is real and measurable: the 1H RSI14 is 84.54 and the 4H is 77.53, both above the 75 threshold this desk treats as overbought for crypto. The 15m has already cooled from 87.28 to 69.41 and its MACD histogram has turned negative at minus 59.51 - the fast frame is unwinding through time rather than price, which is the benign version of a reset.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 80,070.0, RAISED 820.0 points from the 79,250.0 that morning published and never came close to testing. 80,070.1 is the open of the 14:00 UTC hour and the exact low of everything built since the squeeze - the floor of the four-hour consolidation shelf. It sits 709.1 points under the mark, which is 1.27 times the 558.34-point 1H ATR, back inside the 1.2-to-1.3 multiple this file normally uses after morning deliberately widened to 2.05 on an expanding ATR. The tightening is justified because the level is structural rather than statistical: 80,500.0 just below it is the only pure LONG liquidation cluster on the tape at 258,669 USD across 39 fills, so a settled close under 80,070.0 means that shelf has already been harvested and the next real bid is 79,250.0. The settled-close requirement is unchanged and is the rule that has kept this wallet out of six false signals in eleven sessions.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 81,267.0, RAISED from 80,555.4 because that gate fired at 15:00 UTC and has now been defended by three consecutive settled closes. The 17 September lesson recorded in this file is that a trigger which has been paid for is no longer a trigger, so the level moves up to today's high - the price at which the last of the visible short fuel at the 81,000.0 and 81,250.0 buckets was consumed. A settled close above it means the market absorbed 1,870,657 USD of short liquidations and kept going on fresh demand rather than on forced covering, and it opens 81,376.9 and then 81,499.9. What this gate authorises is the SECOND tranche. The first tranche is being taken at market this session at 80,779.1 - deliberately small, because the 1H RSI is 84.54 and this desk does not size up into a vertical frame.

decisionBox.changed: Less changed than this morning, and that is the point - this is a confirmation session, not a repricing one. Bias stays BULLISH and the tilt stays bullish; the probabilities move modestly from 52/30/18 to 56/28/16 and confidence from 6.50 to 6.75. The upgrade is earned by exactly one new fact: open interest is up 4.50 percent to 2,428,535,885 USD since the morning read, so the move is now being funded by new positions rather than by short covering alone. The reduce gate is raised 820.0 points from 79,250.0 to 80,070.0, the floor of the post-squeeze shelf. The add gate is raised 711.6 points from 80,555.4 to 81,267.0, today's high, because the old gate fired and was defended three times. The INVALIDATION is deliberately left at 77,167.3 - morning raised it for the first time this month and moving a structural invalidation twice in two sessions is churn, not discipline. Position moves from TAKE_PROFIT to ADD. Two sessions trimmed roughly 30 percent of the core into this move and price went higher afterwards, which cost about 0.30 USDT of upside but restored 62.78 USDT of cash from 4.02. That cash now has a job.

liquidation.note: 1,376,396 USD across 116 fills and almost purely one-sided - 1,376,251 USD of SHORT liquidations against 146 USD of longs. This is the heaviest bucket on the tape in the 15:16:30 to 17:33:28 UTC window and it is 220.9 points above spot. The honest caveat: price already traded through it to 81,267.0, so this fuel has been burned once. What makes it still a magnet is that it keeps refilling - 116 separate fills means shorts are being re-established into the level and force-covered again, not cleared in a single sweep.

494,261 USD across 112 fills, 100 percent short liquidations. The 81,267.0 session high sits inside this bucket, so it marks the exact ceiling of what the market has been able to pay for. It is 470.9 points above spot.

276,527 USD across 33 fills and the only genuinely two-sided bucket on the tape: 185,830 USD short against 90,697 USD long. Spot at 80,779.1 is trading inside it, which is precisely why the tape is balanced here and why the four-hour range has held - both sides are being stopped out at the same price.

258,669 USD across 39 fills and 100 percent LONG liquidations - the only long-side cluster in the window. It sits 279.1 points under spot and just 68.6 under the last settled hour's low of 80,568.6. This is the air pocket that matters on the downside: it is the leverage that would have to be flushed before the 80,070.0 reduce gate is even reached.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is UP, on both distance and weight, and this is a cleaner read than the balanced call morning had to make. On distance the nearest cluster above is 220.9 points away against 279.1 below. On weight it is not close: 1,870,657 USD of short liquidations sit at 81,000.0 and 81,250.0 against 258,669 USD of long liquidations at 80,500.0, a 7.2-to-1 tilt. The window has cooled a lot from the morning's 38.4-to-1 - total short liquidations are 2,056,342 USD against 349,512 USD of longs over two hours and seventeen minutes, versus 16.3 million USD in eleven minutes this morning - which is what a consolidation looks like rather than an impulse. The forward reading is that the market keeps re-selling into 81,000 and keeps getting paid out, while the only long leverage worth harvesting is a thin shelf at 80,500. This feed is fresh to within twelve minutes of the read and was not stale this run.

liquidations.note: Three readings and all three say the same thing. First, open interest is 2,428,535,885 USD against 2,323,868,439 at the 09:01 COT morning read - up 104.7 million USD and 4.50 percent in under four hours, while price rose 462.5 points. A pure short squeeze DRAINS open interest because shorts are closing; open interest rising alongside price means new capital is being committed. This is the single fact that upgrades the session. Second, realized liquidations over the 15:16:30 to 17:33:28 UTC window are 2,056,342 USD of shorts against 349,512 USD of longs, a 5.9-to-1 skew - still short-dominated but a fraction of the morning's 38.4-to-1, which is the correct signature for a market digesting rather than igniting. Third, the skew field carries the long-short ACCOUNT ratio at 1.01, and its path is the most striking number in this report: 1.54, 1.51, 1.50, 1.46, 1.44, 1.39, 1.37, 1.24, 1.12, 1.05, 1.03, 1.01 over the last twelve hourly readings. Retail accounts have gone from 54 percent net long to dead flat DURING a 5.42 percent rally. That is not distribution into strength by informed money - it is an unloved breakout that the crowd has been selling the whole way up, and crowds that are flat have nothing left to sell. Funding is 0.00991 percent per eight hours, barely positive, with the premium actually NEGATIVE at minus 0.029 percent: perpetual longs are paying almost nothing to hold this, so there is no crowded-leverage tax to unwind.

calibration.note: Morning got the direction right and the wallet action wrong, and both halves deserve to be stated plainly. The directional call: morning published BULLISH at 52 bull against 18 bear with price at 80,316.6, and price is 80,779.1 - 462.5 points and 0.58 percent higher. Correct in sign, which lifts the lifetime line to 99 of 197. Its 79,250.0 reduce gate did NOT fire and was never approached: the lowest trade of the window was 80,070.1, leaving 820.1 points of clearance, and the lowest settled hourly close was 80,728.7 at 1,478.7 points clear. Its 80,555.4 add gate FIRED at 15:00 UTC when that hour settled 80,946.8, clearing by 391.4 points, and was then DEFENDED by two further settled closes at 80,728.7 and 80,849.0 - the strongest confirmation any gate in this file has had. The 77,167.3 invalidation, raised for the first time this month, held with 3,611.8 points of clearance. The late-running midnight report's own 80,632.2 add gate also fired on the same three closes. The discretionary half is the uncomfortable one: morning REDUCED 0.00049772 BTC at 80,316.6 and the late midnight run REDUCED a further 0.00023891 BTC at 80,501.1, trimming about 30 percent of the core into a move that then went 462.5 points higher. The foregone upside is roughly 0.30 USDT across the two trims - 0.23 on the morning tranche and 0.07 on the midnight one - so acting_helped is FALSE on a strict mark-to-market basis. It is worth being honest about the size of that miss rather than defending it: 0.30 USDT is trivial, and what the trims bought was 58.76 USDT of cash against the 4.02 the wallet was carrying. The real error was not this morning's trim, it was the 17 September midday decision to spend down to 4.02 USDT. Selling into strength to restore optionality is a worse trade than never losing the optionality, but it is a much better one than staying frozen.
